tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with 'Diagnose...' which is imperative-adjacent task framing, focuses on the symptoms/intents users will present (access denied, InsufficientCapacityError, no logs, spot interruption restarts, no model package version, deploys not gated, rejected packages, missing lineage, failed MLflow calls), explicitly lists many trigger contexts including ones users wouldn't name directly (e.g. 'bills GPU time for a run with no model'), and also carves out a clear exclusion (not for evaluation jobs). It is a single dense paragraph rather than multiple short sentences, but it remains within the bounds of a short paragraph and stays entirely on user-facing symptoms rather than internal mechanics.
tests.evidence: Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker training or customization job, including Nova and JumpStart fine-tuning, and review Model Registry governance of the models it produces. Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientCapacityError...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific: check-id tables, router mappings, specific API calls, and AWS-specific traps. There's minimal generic explanation of concepts the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: Load checks-sagemaker-training.md before assigning any check-id or severity: the LLM-SM-TRAIN-* and LLM-SM-REG-* sub-family...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps a compact what-it-catches index table and router table but defers full detection rules, remediations and citations to references/checks-sagemaker-training.md and references/collection-reference.md rather than embedding them inline.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference; the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body: checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load

tests.name: Reference path format

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (failure classification, severity assignment, read-only guardrails) are given exact, prescriptive steps, while review scope and area selection allow flexibility with rationale explained.
tests.evidence: Classify **before** prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. ... Every step is **best-effort**

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal choices; it specifies exact APIs/checks to use per scenario in the router table.
tests.evidence: My training job failed ... | `DescribeTrainingJob` `FailureReason`, then the JSONL sample |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and router describe a generalizable approach (classify, confirm, bucket cause, report) applicable to any training job or registry case, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Classify **before** prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.
